posts.heading: September 27, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday recorded 16 species and 234 feeder visits, slightly quieter than the seven-day average of 18.1 species and 288.9 visits. Eastern Towhees and Carolina Chickadees dominated the audio log at 75 and 69 detections respectively. Tufted Titmice logged 85 confident visual visits, beginning 16 minutes before sunrise.

The Red-bellied Woodpecker, recorded every day until yesterday, was absent. This dip in total numbers aligns with a station change on September 26, when a second microphone, c120-extra, began listening alongside the primary unit. No new species were heard exclusively on this source.

Activity stretched from 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with Northern Cardinals providing the final visual record four minutes after sunset. The presence of Blue Jays and House Finches confirmed the station’s usual stability.

posts.heading: September 26, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday recorded 17 species and 284 feeder visits, slightly below the recent baseline of 19.6 species and 278.7 visits. The Eastern Towhee, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal dominated audio detections, while the Tufted Titmouse led in visual presence. A Rose-breasted Grosbeak returned after seven days away.

At 10:44, a second microphone began recording alongside the existing unit, expanding the station’s auditory range. No species were heard for the first time at this station under the new setup.

Visually, the Tufted Titmouse was active from 11 minutes before sunrise and the Northern Cardinal observed as late as 9 minutes after sunset. Mourning Doves were absent, breaking a week-long streak of daily presence. Seed and nectar feeders were recently refilled.

posts.heading: September 25, 2026
posts.text:
The station logged 21 species and 272 feeder visits, exceeding the previous week's average for species count while hearing 281 detections, slightly below the weekly mean. Species diversity peaked yesterday at 19. Regulars such as the Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, and Blue Jay maintained consistent presence, appearing on the visual list alongside the White-breasted Nuthatch and Mourning Dove.

Audio detections highlighted the Northern Cardinal, Carolina Chickadee, and Eastern Towhee, with the Carolina Wren also prominent in the mid-morning hours. The station recorded its first confident visual of the day just 11 minutes before sunrise, featuring a Northern Cardinal, while the last visual sighting was a Blue Jay 20 minutes before sunset. No new species were detected for the first time at the station during this period.

Routine maintenance occurred late in the day, with the seed feeder refilled at 18:22 and the nectar feeder refilled at 18:38. These changes coincided with evening activity, including detections of the Northern Cardinal and Tufted Titmouse in the final hour. A Pileated Woodpecker was detected at 18:00.

posts.heading: September 24, 2026
posts.text:
The station recorded 360 feeder visits, a significant increase over the weekly average of 245.7, while maintaining a species count of 17 that aligns with the recent trend. Regulars such as the Tufted Titmouse, Ruby-throated Hummingbird, and Carolina Chickadee continued their steady presence at the feeders, with Tufted Titmouse visits particularly high at 143. The audio log captured 316 detections, slightly above the weekly mean.

Common Grackle stands out as the first confident visual record at this station, having also been detected by ear for the first time. Other species, including the Eastern Phoebe and Downy Woodpecker, were absent this day. The overall activity level was busier than the preceding seven days, driven largely by the high number of visual visits. The absence of certain regulars like the Song Sparrow and Pileated Woodpecker contrasts with their previous presence.

posts.heading: September 23, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday was a busier day for the station than the recent trend, with 321 feeder visits and 19 species recorded. These totals stand out against the past week's average of 234.7 visits and 18.4 species. The station saw a full complement of regulars, including the Tufted Titmouse, Carolina Chickadee, and Northern Cardinal, which all visited the feeder multiple times.

The audio logs captured a broad range of vocalizations, with the Carolina Chickadee and Northern Cardinal detected most frequently. Several species that were absent earlier in the week, such as the Eastern Phoebe and Red-shouldered Hawk, were heard yesterday.

Visual records confirmed the presence of familiar regulars like the House Finch and Blue Jay, as well as the Mourning Dove. A Tufted Titmouse was also observed perching on the rim of a treat bowl during its visits.

posts.heading: September 22, 2026
posts.text:
Feeder traffic doubled the weekly average, with 428 visits compared to a mean of 213.3 over the past week. Tufted Titmice dominated the activity log with 203 visits, while House Finches and Northern Cardinals also showed increased presence. The total number of species detected was slightly lower than the recent average.

The roster remained consistent with the previous week, including daily regulars like the Carolina Wren and Eastern Towhee. A Cedar Waxwing appeared, marking its first visit in seven days. Eastern Phoebes, typically a daily presence, were absent.

Audio detections were quieter than the weekly norm, totaling 251 compared to an average of 295.0.

posts.heading: September 21, 2026
posts.text:
Yesterday registered 124 feeder visits, a notably quiet day compared to the 230.0 average of the previous week. The species count of 17 held steady against the 17.3 weekly average. All core regulars, including the Tufted Titmouse and Carolina Chickadee, were present.

The Tufted Titmouse provided the first and last visual records of the day, visiting the tube feeder 12 minutes before sunrise and 21 minutes before sunset. The species' consistent daily attendance was observed for the seventh consecutive day.

Missing from the log were several species recorded earlier in the week, including the Red-shouldered Hawk and White-eyed Vireo.
